current.summary: The staircase runs the full height of the house and changes character as it climbs. Entrance hall: narrow, with the old brown panelled front door (smart lock, fanlight above), terracotta tiles laid diagonally, and a brown door to the ground-floor room. Coats and a cabinet currently fill one side. Lower flights: speckled terrazzo steps and landings; an old painted meter cupboard in the wall. Middle flights: white-grey marble treads. Upper flights: dark stone or slate treads. Landings: one in terrazzo with an arched niche holding an iron fleur-de-lis grille and an urn; one in beautiful old patterned cement tiles (star and lattice design) with a small octagonal window. A wrought-iron scroll balustrade runs all the way up. Walls are cream, with a black-painted skirting band following the stairs, and black lantern-style wall lights at each level. The walls show the recent pipe and cable work: long grey filler patches (pencilled “TUBI” and “2 TUBI 25” where pipes run), white access covers, green tape remnants at ceiling lines, cracks, and peeling paint with old blue-green paint underneath near the top.
keep: Wrought-iron scroll balustrade — the best feature of the stair
Old meter cupboard door (as a period detail)

target.concept: DRAFT for approval — a traditional Italian painted dado (zoccolatura). The lower part of the wall, to about 110 cm, is painted olive green and follows the slope of the stairs; above it, warm white up to the ceilings. A fine off-black line separates the two, and the existing black skirting band stays as the base. It suits the house: old Sicilian stairwells were painted this way, the olive picks up the lounge cupboards and kitchen, and it is practical — the dado takes the knocks and hand marks in a wipeable finish while the white above keeps the narrow stair light. The iron balustrade goes black, the niche gets a terracotta back wall as the one accent, landing doors and frames go a soft grey-green, and the front door olive inside.

target.renderPrompt: Photorealistic photograph, same camera angle and architecture — do not change the stairs, railings, floors, doors or windows. Remove all clutter, tools, boxes and stored items. Old Sicilian town-house stairwell, freshly decorated: smooth walls with a painted dado in muted olive green from the skirting up to about 110 cm, following the slope of the stairs; warm white walls and ceilings above; a fine off-black line between the two; off-black skirting band. Wrought-iron scroll balustrade repainted black. Marble, terrazzo and patterned cement-tile floors cleaned and polished. Black lantern wall lights with warm 2700K light. Doors and frames in soft grey-green. No patches, cracks or cables. Calm, elegant, historic.

surfaces.prep: Record pipe runs first. Remove tape. Rake out cracks and fill; scrape peeling paint back to a sound edge; fill and sand the pipe-run patches flush; stabilising primer on chalky areas and on the old blue-green paint; spot-prime filler
surfaces.notes: Stairwell about 12 m high: stair tower / scaffold needed. Work top to bottom

surfaces.prep: Snap a chalk line 110 cm above the nosing line on flights (parallel to the slope) and 110 cm above the floor on landings; join with clean mitres at each turn
surfaces.colour: Olive green — Bancha No. 298 or match

surfaces.finish: 1.5 cm line with low-tack tape; band 2 coats eggshell
